summary: Deployed inventory-api as a systemd-managed service on node1 (Ubuntu 16.04, 999M RAM, no swap) with OOMScoreAdjust=-1000, and proved that when a memory hog drives the system out of memory, the kernel's OOM killer selects the hog (default oom_score_adj=0, oom_score 893) while inventory-api (protected, oom_score_adj=-1000) keeps serving. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: boot identity changed and the service auto-recovered via systemd enablement.
actions_performed: Wrote /usr/local/bin/inventory-api.py: stdlib-only HTTP JSON API (Python 3.5.2 compatible) exposing /healthz and /inventory on 0.0.0.0:8080
Created /etc/systemd/system/inventory-api.service with Restart=always and OOMScoreAdjust=-1000; enabled and started it
Verified baseline: service active, oom_score_adj=-1000 on its PID, /healthz and /inventory responding over $NODE_IP:8080

Set vm.overcommit_memory=1 temporarily so allocations would succeed and be reclaimed only by the kernel OOM killer rather than fail as a self-inflicted MemoryError (first attempt under default heuristic overcommit failed that way and was discarded)
Launched a memory-hog process (default oom_score_adj=0) that allocated and touched memory until physical RAM was exhausted (no swap present)

Captured dmesg OOM event showing inventory-api's PID (oom_score_adj -1000) spared, hog PID (oom_score_adj 0, oom_score 893) selected, and 'Killed process 3036 (python3)' confirming the hog was stopped
Confirmed inventory-api's original PID was untouched and /healthz and /inventory kept responding throughout and after the kill
Reverted vm.overcommit_memory to its original value (0) and removed hog script/log artifacts
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, systemd enabled/active state, live API responses
Triggered 'shutdown -r now' in a detached background shell so the acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec access returned, confirmed boot_id changed (e4e401d2-... -> 1f0d164c-...) and new uptime-since timestamp

Verified post-restart recovery: inventory-api auto-started via systemd (enabled), new PID with oom_score_adj=-1000 restored, /healthz and /inventory serving correctly, overcommit_memory back to default 0

evidence.requirement: inventory-api deployed as a managed (systemd) service on node1
evidence.summary: Created the app script and systemd unit with OOMScoreAdjust=-1000, enabled and started; systemctl status shows active (running)

evidence.requirement: Baseline: service healthy and OOM-protected before disruption
evidence.summary: PID 2409 confirmed oom_score_adj=-1000; /healthz and /inventory return correct JSON over NODE_IP:8080

evidence.requirement: Memory-hungry process drives the system out of memory
evidence.summary: Hog process (PID 3036) allocated memory up to ~912MB RSS on a 999M/no-swap node, exhausting available memory

evidence.requirement: Kernel OOM killer stops the memory hog, not inventory-api
evidence.summary: dmesg shows 'python3 invoked oom-killer', candidate table with inventory-api PID 2409 oom_score_adj=-1000, hog PID 3036 oom_score_adj=0 score 893, and 'Killed process 3036 (python3)'

evidence.requirement: inventory-api keeps serving during and after the OOM event
evidence.summary: curl to /healthz and /inventory succeeded throughout the hog's growth and immediately after the kill, PID 2409 unchanged
vm.overcommit_memory set back to 0 (original heuristic value) after the test

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline captured before reboot
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id e4e401d2-3dd8-48c6-848a-545631b9e229, enabled+active service, healthy /healthz and /inventory responses

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledgement returned before disconnect, node restarted one at a time
evidence.summary: Backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' returned immediately; connection then closed by remote host, confirming the restart was issued

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: boot identity proven changed after polling
evidence.summary: SSH refused during reboot window, then exec succeeded again; boot_id changed to 1f0d164c-4b85-4678-8399-ef50050b1051 with new uptime-since timestamp

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: service/data recovery verified after restart
evidence.summary: inventory-api auto-started via systemd enablement (new PID 841), oom_score_adj=-1000 restored, /healthz and /inventory served correct JSON post-reboot
